events.label: Watson describes Holmes as untidy in personal habits

communicates.speaker: watson
communicates.content: as he had finished pasting extracts into his common-place book, he might employ the next two hours in making our room a little more habitable

events.label: Holmes goes to his bedroom and returns with a large tin box
Holmes opens the tin box and reveals bundles of papers
Holmes says the box contains cases and early work records

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: There are cases enough here, Watson. I think that if you knew all that I had in this box you would ask me to pull some out instead of putting others in. Yes, my boy, these were all done prematurely before my biographer had come to glorify me. They are not all successes, Watson. But there are some pretty little problems among them. Here's the record of the Tarleton murders, and the case of Vamberry, the wine merchant, and the adventure of the old Russian woman, and the singular affair of the aluminium crutch, as well as a full account of Ricoletti of the club-foot, and his abominable wife. And here—ah, now, this really is something a little recherché.

events.label: Holmes dives into the chest and brings up a small wooden box
Holmes produces a crumpled piece of paper, a brass key, a peg of wood with string, and three rusty disks from the box
Holmes arranges the objects along the edge of the table
Holmes sits back and looks over the objects with satisfaction
Holmes identifies the objects as all that he has left from the adventure of the Musgrave Ritual

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: These are all that I have left to remind me of the adventure of the Musgrave Ritual.

events.label: Watson asks Holmes to give an account of the case

communicates.speaker: watson
communicates.content: I should be so glad if you would give me an account of it.

events.label: Holmes asks Watson whether he should leave the litter as it is

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: And leave the litter as it is?

events.label: Holmes says Watson's tidiness will not bear much strain

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Your tidiness won't bear much strain after all, Watson.

events.label: Holmes says the case should be added to Watson's annals and calls it unique

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: I should be glad that you should add this case to your annals, for there are points in it which make it quite unique in the criminal records of this or, I believe, of any other country. A collection of my trifling achievements would certainly be incomplete which contained no account of this very singular business.

events.label: Holmes describes how earlier cases turned his attention to his profession

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: The affair of the Gloria Scott and my conversation with the unhappy man whose fate I told you of first turned my attention in the direction of the profession which has become my life's work. You see me now when my name has become known far and wide.

events.label: Holmes says he had rooms in Montague Street and studied science there

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: When I first came up to London I had rooms in Montague Street, just round the corner from the British Museum, and there I waited, filling in my too abundant leisure time by studying all those branches of science which might make me more efficient.

events.label: Holmes says cases came to him through old fellow-students

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Now and again cases came in my way, principally through the introduction of old fellow-students.

events.label: Holmes says the Musgrave Ritual was his third such case

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: The third of these cases was that of the Musgrave Ritual.

events.label: Holmes describes Reginald Musgrave as a college acquaintance

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Reginald Musgrave had been in the same college as myself, and I had some slight acquaintance with him.

events.label: Holmes and Reginald Musgrave converse occasionally
Reginald Musgrave walks into Watson's room in Montague Street.
Reginald Musgrave and Watson cordially shake hands.
Reginald Musgrave speaks to Watson about his father's death, his management of the Hurlstone estates, and his role as member for his district.

communicates.speaker: reginald_musgrave
communicates.content: You probably heard of my poor father's death; he was carried off about two years ago. Since then I have had the Hurlstone estates to manage, and as I am member for my district as well, my life has been a busy one.

events.label: Reginald Musgrave says that strange doings have occurred at Hurlstone and that the police have thrown no light on the matter.

communicates.speaker: reginald_musgrave
communicates.content: I am delighted to hear it, for your advice at present would be exceedingly valuable to me. We have had some very strange doings at Hurlstone, and the police have been able to throw no light upon the matter. It is really the most extraordinary and inexplicable business.

events.label: Watson listens eagerly to Reginald Musgrave.
Watson asks for the details.

communicates.speaker: watson
communicates.content: Pray, let me have the details.

events.label: Reginald Musgrave sits down opposite Watson and lights a cigarette.
Reginald Musgrave describes the staff at Hurlstone and names Brunton as the longest-serving servant.

communicates.speaker: reginald_musgrave
communicates.content: Though I am a bachelor, I have to keep up a considerable staff of servants at Hurlstone, for it is a rambling old place, and takes a good deal of looking after. I preserve, too, and in the pheasant months I usually have a house-party, so that it would not do to be short-handed. Altogether there are eight maids, the cook, the butler, two footmen, and a boy. The garden and the stables of course have a separate staff. Of these servants the one who had been longest in our service was Brunton the butler.

events.label: Reginald Musgrave describes Brunton as a former schoolmaster who became valuable in the household and had worked there for twenty years.

communicates.speaker: reginald_musgrave
communicates.content: He was a young schoolmaster out of place when he was first taken up by my father, but he was a man of great energy and character, and he soon became quite invaluable in the household. He was a well-grown, handsome man, with a splendid forehead, and though he has been with us for twenty years he cannot be more than forty now. With his personal advantages and his extraordinary gifts—it is wonderful that he should have been satisfied so long in such a position.

events.label: Reginald Musgrave describes Brunton's romantic behavior, engagement to Rachel Howells, and later involvement with Janet Tregellis.

communicates.speaker: reginald_musgrave
communicates.content: This paragon has one fault. He is a bit of a Don Juan. When he was married it was all right, but since he has been a widower we have had no end of trouble with him. A few months ago we were in hopes that he was about to settle down again for he became engaged to Rachel Howells, our second housemaid; but he has thrown her over since then and taken up with Janet Tregellis, the daughter of the head gamekeeper. Rachel had a sharp touch of brain-fever, and goes about the house now—or did until yesterday—like a black-eyed shadow of her former self. That was our first drama at Hurlstone; but a second one came to drive it from our minds, and it was prefaced by the disgrace and dismissal of butler Brunton.

communicates.speaker: watson

events.label: Watson relocks the bureau and is interrupted by the returned butler
Brunton pleads to avoid public disgrace and asks to resign with notice

communicates.speaker: brunton
communicates.content: Mr. Musgrave, sir, I can't bear disgrace, sir. I've always been proud above my station in life, and disgrace would kill me. My blood will be on your head, sir—it will, indeed—if you drive me to despair. If you cannot keep me after what has passed, then for God's sake let me give you notice and leave in a month, as if of my own free will. I could stand that, Mr. Musgrave, but not to be cast out before all the folk that I know so well.

events.label: Musgrave dismisses Brunton within a week

communicates.speaker: reginald_musgrave
communicates.content: You don't deserve much consideration, Brunton. Your conduct has been most infamous. However, as you have been a long time in the family, I have no wish to bring public disgrace upon you. A month, however is too long. Take yourself away in a week, and give what reason you like for going. A week, and you may consider yourself to have been very leniently dealt with.

events.label: Brunton leaves crestfallen and Musgrave returns to his room
Brunton serves dutifully for two days
Brunton fails to appear after breakfast on the third morning
Watson meets Rachel Howells and urges her to rest

communicates.speaker: watson
communicates.content: You should be in bed. Come back to your duties when you are stronger.

communicates.speaker: rachel_howells
communicates.content: I am strong enough, Mr. Musgrave.

events.label: Watson says the doctor will decide and tells her to stop work and request Brunton

communicates.speaker: watson
communicates.content: We will see what the doctor says. You must stop work now, and when you go downstairs just say that I wish to see Brunton.

communicates.speaker: rachel_howells
communicates.content: The butler is gone. Gone where? He is gone. No one has seen him. He is not in his room. Oh, yes, he is gone, he is gone!

Watson asks to see the paper that the butler consulted

communicates.speaker: watson
communicates.content: I must see that paper, Musgrave, which this butler of yours thought it worth his while to consult, even at the risk of the loss of his place.

events.label: Musgrave describes the ritual as absurd but ancient and offers a copy of the questions and answers

communicates.speaker: reginald_musgrave
communicates.content: It is rather an absurd business, this ritual of ours. But it has at least the saving grace of antiquity to excuse it. I have a copy of the questions and answers here if you care to run your eye over them.

events.label: Holmes reads the Musgrave Ritual questions and answers aloud

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Whose was it? His who is gone. Who shall have it? He who will come. Where was the sun? Over the oak. Where was the shadow? Under the elm. How was it stepped? North by ten and by ten, east by five and by five, south by two and by two, west by one and by one, and so under. What shall we give for it? All that is ours. Why should we give it? For the sake of the trust.

events.label: Musgrave remarks on the ritual manuscript

communicates.speaker: reginald_musgrave
communicates.content: The original has no date, but is in the spelling of the middle of the seventeenth century. It can be of little help in solving this mystery.

events.label: Holmes comments on the paper and Brunton's interest in it

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: It gives us another mystery, and one which may solve the first. Your butler appears to have been a very clever man. The paper seems to be of practical importance. Brunton probably saw it before that night. He had probably seen it again to refresh his memory. He had some sort of map or chart which he was comparing with the manuscript, and he thrust it into his pocket when you appeared. I don't think we should have much difficulty in determining that.

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes

communicates.speaker: reginald_musgrave
communicates.content: There used to be a very old one over yonder but it was struck by lightning ten years ago, and we cut down the stump. No old ones, but plenty of beeches.

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: I should like to see where it grew.

communicates.speaker: reginald_musgrave
communicates.content: It was nearly midway between the oak and the house.

communicates.speaker: reginald_musgrave
communicates.content: It was sixty-four feet.

communicates.speaker: reginald_musgrave
communicates.content: When my old tutor used to give me an exercise in trigonometry, it always took the shape of measuring heights. When I was a lad I worked out every tree and building in the estate.

communicates.speaker: reginald_musgrave
communicates.content: Brunton did ask me about the height of the tree some months ago, in connection with some little argument with the groom.

Holmes states that he had been disappointed in his investigation

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: I had been disappointed in my investigation. I had reckoned upon solving the matter when once I had found the place referred to in the Ritual; but now I was there, and was apparently as far as ever from knowing what it was which the family had concealed with such elaborate precautions. It is true that I had thrown a light upon the fate of Brunton, but now I had to ascertain how that fate had come upon him, and what part had been played in the matter by the woman who had disappeared.

communicates.speaker: musgrave_ritual
communicates.content: These are coins of Charles the First; you see we were right in fixing our date for the Ritual.

events.label: Musgrave and Watson go up to the study and he lays the debris before Watson
Watson examines the debris, rubs a stone, and observes it glow
Watson explains the historical interpretation of the relic

communicates.speaker: watson
communicates.content: You must bear in mind that the Royal party made head in England even after the death of the King, and that when they at last fled they probably left many of their most precious possessions buried behind them, with the intention of returning for them in more peaceful times. My ancestor, Sir Ralph Musgrave, was a prominent Cavalier and the right-hand man of Charles the Second in his wanderings. Well now, I think that really should give us the last link that we wanted. I must congratulate you on coming into the possession, though in rather a tragic manner of a relic which is of great intrinsic value, but of even greater importance as an historical curiosity. It is nothing less than the ancient crown of the Kings of England.

events.label: Holmes explains the Musgrave Ritual's questions and answers

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Consider what the Ritual says: 'Whose was it?' 'His who is gone.' That was after the execution of Charles. Then, 'Who shall have it?' 'He who will come.' That was Charles the Second, whose advent was already foreseen. There can, I think, be no doubt that this battered and shapeless diadem once encircled the brows of the royal Stuarts.

events.label: Watson asks how the crown came into the pond

communicates.speaker: watson
communicates.content: And how came it in the pond?

events.label: Holmes narrates his chain of surmise and proof

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: And with that I sketched out to him the whole long chain of surmise and of proof which I had constructed.

events.label: Musgrave asks about the relic's return

communicates.speaker: reginald_musgrave
communicates.content: And when he returned?

events.label: Holmes explains the secret may have been lost through inheritance

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: It is likely that the Musgrave who held the secret died in the interval, and by some oversight left this guide to his descendant without explaining the meaning of it. From that day to this it has been handed down from father to son, until at last it came within reach of a man who tore its secret out of it and lost his life in the venture.

events.label: Holmes states that the story of the Musgrave Ritual is complete

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: And that's the story of the Musgrave Ritual, Watson.

events.label: Holmes says the crown is kept at Hurlstone

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: They have the crown down at Hurlstone—though they had some legal bother and a considerable sum to pay before they were allowed to retain it. I am sure that if you mentioned my name they would be happy to show it to you.

events.label: Holmes states that the woman escaped from England

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Of the woman nothing was ever heard, and the probability is that she got away out of England and carried herself and the memory of her crime to some land beyond the seas.
